name: CDL Air Brakes
officialName: Commercial Driver's License (CDL) Air Brakes Test
trademarkNotice: This practice resource is independent and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by any state Department of Motor Vehicles or driver licensing agency, the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA), or the American Association of Motor Vehicle Administrators (AAMVA). Agency names are used only to identify the test this material helps you prepare for.

examInfo.format: Multiple choice questions on the Air Brakes section of your state's CDL manual (Section 5 in the common manual layout). You take this test if the vehicle you will drive has air brakes, including air-over-hydraulic brakes. Many states, such as Washington, use 25 questions, and some state manuals, such as New York's, say each question has three answer choices. States do not all publish a time limit, so this practice mock uses 25 questions, 30 minutes, and 3 answer choices per question.

passCriteria.description: Federal rules require at least 80% correct on every CDL knowledge test. On a 25-question test, that means at least 20 correct answers, so you can miss no more than 5.

content.eligibility: You take the Air Brakes test along with the CDL General Knowledge test when you apply for a commercial learner's permit (CLP). You need a valid regular driver license, must meet your state's age and medical rules, and must pass the General Knowledge test as well. Check your state's driver licensing agency for the exact documents and fees.
content.intro: The CDL Air Brakes test checks that you understand how air brakes work, how to inspect them, and how to use them safely. You must take it if the commercial vehicle you will drive has air brakes, including air-over-hydraulic brakes. If you do not pass it, or you take your skills test in a vehicle without air brakes, your license gets an air brake restriction, and you cannot drive a commercial vehicle with full air brakes. The test is based on the Air Brakes section of your state's CDL manual.
content.trendSummary: Questions focus on the parts of the system and the numbers in the manual: governor cut-in and cut-out pressures, the safety valve setting, the low-air warning before 60 psi, spring brakes coming on between 20 and 45 psi, the air build-up rate, and the leakage limits. Stopping distance and brake lag, the downgrade braking method, and what to do when the low-air warning comes on also come up often. The chapters on this site follow the manual but are study groupings, not official test sections.
content.studyTip: Start with Parts of an Air Brake System, because every other topic uses those words. Then learn the inspection checks with their numbers on one list (psi, seconds, and minutes) and review it daily. Finish with Using Air Brakes, where the downgrade method and brake lag are common questions. Before test day, take a full 25-question Mock Exam and aim for 23 or more.

faqs.question: What score do I need to pass the CDL Air Brakes test?
faqs.answer: Federal rules require at least 80% correct on every CDL knowledge test. On a 25-question test that means at least 20 correct answers. Some states may use a different number of questions, but the 80% rule is the same everywhere.

faqs.question: Do I need the Air Brakes test?
faqs.answer: You need it if you will drive a commercial vehicle with air brakes, including air-over-hydraulic brakes. If you do not pass it, your license will have an air brake restriction. Most tractor-trailers and many large trucks and buses have air brakes.

faqs.question: Which part of the CDL manual should I study?
faqs.answer: Study the Air Brakes section, which is Section 5 in the common CDL manual layout. Your state may also tell you to read the introduction and the general knowledge sections. Check your own state's manual for the exact list.

faqs.question: Are these the real CDL test questions?
faqs.answer: No. The real question banks are not public. Every question here is an original practice question written from the rules in state CDL manuals. Use this site to learn the rules, and read your state's official CDL manual as well.

studyTips.studyOrder: Start with Parts of an Air Brake System. It is the largest chapter on this site (35%) and every other chapter uses its words, like governor, slack adjuster, and spring brakes. Next study Inspecting Air Brake Systems (30%) and Using Air Brakes (25%). Finish with Dual Air Brake Systems, which is short.
studyTips.hardChapters: Inspecting Air Brake Systems has many numbers that look alike, such as the leakage limits for single and combination vehicles with the brakes released and applied. Put them in one table and review it daily. Parts of an Air Brake System is easy to mix up when it comes to pressures: the governor cut-in and cut-out, the safety valve, the low-air warning, and the spring brakes each have their own number.
studyTips.examDay: You need at least 80% to pass, which is 20 correct answers out of 25, so you can miss no more than 5 questions. Read all three answer choices before you choose, because wrong choices often change only one number. When two choices look right, pick the one that matches the exact number in the manual.
